reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not report coercivity values for the baseline or RTA-treated films, nor does it mention a 40-fold increase or a single-phase fcc pattern after RTA. E2 shows RTA on films grown at 20 °C, not 350 °C, and describes phase separation at higher temperatures, contradicting the premise of suppressing secondary phases. The key premises are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: RTA at 600 °C for 30 s induces a high anisotropy phase in FeCoNiMnCu films.
The high anisotropy phase formation increases coercivity by ~40-fold.
The baseline as-grown film at 350 °C has a coercivity of 10 Oe.
RTA suppresses secondary phase growth and yields a single-phase fcc pattern.
